scope: Post-freeze semantic/function validation of already discovered rRNA primitives.

published_Ecoli_23S_segment.source: Oldenburg/Zhang et al., Sequence specific detection of bacterial 23S ribosomal RNA by TLR13, eLife 2012, DOI 10.7554/eLife.00102

numbering_anchor.derivation: LC-PRIM-0006 contains ACGGAAAGACCC as bases 6-17. Aligning that exact 12-nt substring to published 23S positions 2054-2065 places LC-PRIM-0006 at E. coli 23S positions 2049-2065. Frozen start-to-start spacings then place LC-PRIM-0003 at 1930-1945 and LC-PRIM-0007 at 560-583. LC-PRIM-0002 begins four bases before LC-PRIM-0003, placing it at 1926-1949, independently agreeing with its published name Uni23S1926F.
numbering_anchor.evidence_class: E1 deterministic positional mapping using a published sequence anchor plus previously frozen exact spacings

LC-PRIM-0007.claim: Positions 560-583 straddle the structure-based Domain I / Domain 0 boundary; Domain 0 includes 562-586 and is described as the central highly conserved core that provides structural integrity to 23S rRNA.
sources: Petrov et al. 2013, Nucleic Acids Research 41:7522-7535, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkt513

LC-PRIM-0003.claim: Positions 1930-1945 lie in the highly conserved Domain IV region at the large/small subunit interface near the peptidyl-transferase center.
sources: Everett & Dahlberg 1995, J Mol Biol, PMID 7784204
Everett et al. / Chlamydiales 23S intron study, PMCID PMC93955

LC-PRIM-0003.claim: The primitive includes U1940. U1940A was experimentally reported to produce 50S subunits defective in subunit-subunit association while retaining peptidyl-transferase activity.

LC-PRIM-0006.claim: The primitive spans positions 2049-2065 and contains positions A2058 and G2061 in the 23S rRNA catalytic/antibiotic-recognition neighborhood.

The published 2054-2068 sequence is a sequence-specific TLR13 ligand; the paper places it in Domain V at the catalytic center, identifies G2061 as an invariant catalytic-region residue, and notes that A2058 modification is associated with macrolide resistance.

interpretation_boundary: The literature establishes structural/mechanistic context for these positions. Coder-style aliases below are I1 abstractions and are not claimed as literal biochemical opcode names.
